items.fact: climbing season window
items.prior_evidence: Documented ascents span mid-May (on snow), June (2001, 2005, 2013) and September (2015, 2019); none found in October and no source states a window. The season chip (Jun-Sep) and the July-October best_season / seasonal_guidance / approach-variant window ('July to early October') still disagree at both ends, and no two sources settle either end.

items.fact: number/type of summit rappels
items.prior_evidence: No new count: a 2013 first-hand report mentions a rappel with 'double overhangs' but no number or rope; another report used 60 m of rope as a hand line. Earlier accounts (one double-rope rap; two raps on 2x30 m; three raps on a single 60 m) still disagree, so rappels, descent_text and climbing_route[3] cannot be reconciled on two agreeing sources.

items.fact: one-way / round-trip approach distance
items.prior_evidence: No source found states a one-way mileage to the base or a 3-day total; stated round trips remain 16, 16.5, ~17 and ~18 mi from different parties and camps. The waypoint distMi values and the 19-20 mi 3-day total cannot be sourced, and halving is not a stated figure.

items.fact: Total elevation gain/loss
items.prior_evidence: No additional cumulative gain found; figures remain 8,000, ~7,300, ~7,400 and 6,972 ft (net) from different reports, no two equal. gain_ft 8,000, loss_ft 6,995 and the itinerary's ~7,200 are left for a decision.

items.fact: Approach mileage/gain figures citing the wrong route's trailhead (Scatter Lake)
items.prior_evidence: Still real: partner_requirements quotes the south-side Scatter Lake figures (~11 mi RT / 5,200 ft) beside a Wolf Creek figure, and approachTime mixes both. These figures cannot be replaced until the row's approach is rebuilt around the Wolf Creek/Gardner Meadows line (see the STRUCTURAL item below). A 2020 Wolf Creek report gives only '10-ish miles' to Gardner Meadows and 4.25 hours, which is not a stated car-to-car distance/gain; no second source gives one, so nothing is patched.

items.fact: Which approach/trailhead the North Ridge uses (North Creek Trail #413 + mine trail vs Wolf Creek/Gardner Meadows; Trailhead waypoint named Scatter Creek at 3,150 ft)
items.prior_evidence: STRUCTURAL: rebuild the row around the Wolf Creek / Gardner Meadows approach (decision rule 3: most documented line in current use). Two independent trip reports climb the north ridge this way: a July 2020 report (Wolf Creek trail ~10 mi to Gardner Meadows, off-trail past Abernathy Lake to the tarn below the ridge, spur ridge with a few class 3 moves to the main ridge, boot path through old mining remains, class 2/3 to the summit) and a separate multi-peak report from Wolf Creek via Gardner Meadows, the abandoned mine trail and tarn. The North Creek Trail #413 mine-trail approach is described by only one source (the peak's main route page). What should change: move the Trailhead waypoint (currently named 'Scatter Creek Trailhead' with a North Creek note, 3,150 ft) to the Wolf Creek Trailhead; rewrite approach, approach_logistics.trailhead/trailheadDirection, itinerary day 1, timing.sectionBreakdown note, pro_tips[0] ('via the Twisp River side') and partner_requirements to the Gardner Meadows line; demote the North Creek text to an approach_variants alternative or drop it. Needs pin moves and a whole-row rewrite, which the patch format cannot express.

items.fact: Pass-to-summit distance: beta/pitch_detail 0.4 mi vs waypoint distMi 7.4 -> 8.5 (1.1 mi)
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. New reports give time and gain, not distance, for the pass-to-summit leg: a 2020 GPS-timed party went Fish Creek Pass to the summit in 45 min (pass at 6.94 mi, then 9.92 mi after a Star Peak side trip, with no Courtney mileage), a 2023 report calls it steep but short at almost 900 ft, and a Bulger-list report says 45 min to an hour. The trail database gives the trail as 7.4 mi to the pass. No source states a pass-to-summit mileage, so neither 0.4 mi nor the waypoints' 1.1 mi can be adopted.

items.fact: Published approach time 4 hr vs itinerary 5-6 hr to Fish Creek Pass
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. Two dated trailhead-to-pass times were found, and they disagree with each other and with both row figures in different ways: a 2020 GPS-timed day party took 3 h 05 min (04:00 to 07:05) and a 2023 day hiker on snow took about 4 h. Both are light day-pack times; neither addresses the itinerary's 32 lb overnight pack, and no two sources give the same figure, so neither approachTimeHrs 4 nor the schedule's +5 to 6 hr is changed.

items.fact: Total pitch count
items.prior_evidence: Still real: pitches 20 vs ~18 pitches in overview, pro_tips, totalNote and partner fields. Pitch counts for the Complete vs Upper North Ridge are not a stable published figure (most parties simul-climb the lower ridge) and no two independent sources agree on one number; decision rule 2 covers grades, not pitch counts. No new source on this pass.

items.fact: Trailhead pin vs the approach the waypoints and itinerary describe
items.prior_evidence: STRUCTURAL: waypoints[1] 'Longs Pass' (distMi 3.5) and waypoints[2] 'Goat Pass' (distMi 5) are south-approach (Esmeralda / Ingalls Creek) pins placed in the chain that starts at waypoints[0], the Stuart Lake Trailhead on the north side; their distances from that trailhead are meaningless. The primary approach in approach, approach_logistics and approach_variants[0] is the north side via Mountaineer Creek, which is also how the two most detailed ascent reports approach the North Ridge. Fix: remove Longs Pass and Goat Pass from this route's waypoint list (or move them to a south-variant list), keeping the Stuart Lake Trailhead pin; this needs a pin/list change the patch format cannot express.

items.fact: Elevation gain to the crag
items.prior_evidence: The live row changed since the earlier passes: the trailhead pin now sits at the FS 9070 left-fork road end at 4,254 ft and the crag pin at 4,650 ft, so the row's own waypoints now show ~400 ft of net rise against gain_ft 750 (the ground heights, ~4,250 ft at the road end and ~4,670 ft at the crag, agree). But net relief is only a floor for cumulative gain, so 750 is not provably wrong, and no published source states the approach gain for the Silver Basin / Citadel crags (area pages give only the 20-30 minute walk). A gain figure from pin heights would be computed. No patch.

items.fact: Season / when the access road is open
items.prior_evidence: Still split between the only two statements found: one hiking guide says FR-9070 is generally snow-free from July until November; the Silver Peak route page gives June-October as the window while FR-9070 is open to the public. A third search (other Silver Peak and Olallie Meadow pages) gave road directions but no opening month. The sources disagree on June vs July, so no window is adopted.

items.fact: Whole-outing gain/loss: gain_ft 6257 vs loss_ft 6157 on an out-and-back, with day 2 not counting the re-climb over Fourth Creek Pass
items.prior_evidence: New sources this pass: a single-day ascent from the Beverly Creek trailhead gives c.15 mi round trip but only the net 4,853 ft rise, and an archived route page gives the Beverly/Fourth Creek approach as about 5.1 mi with ~1,800 ft up to Fourth Creek Pass and ~1,200 ft down to Ingalls Creek (to be re-climbed on return). Neither states a car-to-car gain, and the only stated figures (7,400 ft; ~7,550 ft assembled from one report's day figures) are not two agreeing stated totals. New day-2 values would have to be computed, so nothing is patched.

items.fact: Which trailhead/approach the route uses (Alpental vs Denny Creek)
items.prior_evidence: STRUCTURAL: the Southeast Slopes line starts at the Denny Creek trailhead (~2,300 ft, I-90 Exit 47) and leaves the Denny Creek Trail #1014 at Hemlock Pass, as the row's approach, itinerary and primary variant already say; a 2013 trip page gives 'via Denny Creek + Hemlock Pass', 10.8 mi RT, 2,280-5,801 ft, and a club route page (search excerpt) describes the same Hemlock Pass line on a 33° bearing. What should change: approach_logistics.trailhead/trailheadLat/trailheadLng/trailheadDirection and waypoint 0 re-pointed to the Denny Creek trailhead (coordinates too), and waypoints 1-6 (Source Lake junction, stream crossing, gully passage, Thumbtack, Bryant-Chair gully) removed from this route or moved to the Alpental variant — they trace the secondary gully line. Waypoint 0's note already names Denny Creek while its name/coords are Alpental. Pin moves are outside the patch format.

items.fact: Summit-day gain 3,080 ft reaches the 7,727 ft central summit, not the 7,440 ft South Peak this row climbs
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. Still real: day 2 gains/loses 3,080 ft from the 4,650 ft Sunrise Knob camp, exactly the camp-to-main-summit difference, while this row ends on the 7,440 ft South Peak. The one South Peak trip report found (East Gully, from Sunrise Knob at 4,650 ft) gives only whole-trip stats of 19 mi and 5,000 ft gained and lost, and times (4.9 h up, 3.1 h down) with no summit-day gain; an archived route page gives 3,100 ft from the bivy basin but to the main summit. No source states the camp-to-South-Peak gain, and a figure from pin heights would be computed, so no patch.

items.fact: Summit-day length and start time: partner_requirements vs timing/itinerary
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. The archived peak page gives the Northeast Couloir only as Grade II or III, steep couloir to 60 degrees, winter/early-spring route, with no times; the reports that surface for camp departures (4:30 AM) and lake approaches (5-6 h in snow) concern the neighbouring North Buttress Couloir. No source states a camp-to-camp time or a start time for this couloir, so neither partner_requirements' 04:00 / 8.5 h nor timing's 2:30 AM / 11 h can be adopted.

items.fact: Day-2 climb duration
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. Searches (route listing, web, and the forum archive for a 2006 first-ascent report) still turn up no ascent account of Der Dihedral with any time; the only figures remain the Backbone Ridge/NE Arete proxies (about 12 h of climbing, 13-14 h camp to camp), which favour the schedule's 3:30 AM-7:00 PM (15.5 h) over hours/summitTimeHrs 11 and the totalNote's 10-12 h but are for a different start. With no route-specific source, nothing is changed.

items.fact: Total trip time vs its own approach/summit/descent legs
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. The peak's long-standing route page gives two to three days from Diablo to Elephant Butte with heavy packs (~10 mi one way) or one long day travelling light, with no hours; the new solo account found reached the Stetattle Ridge high point at 3 h 50 min elapsed with 3-5 mi and 2,500+ ft still to go, while earlier reports give ~10 h from a ridge camp to the summit and back, or 10-12 h each way with overnight packs. These do not agree on leg times or a total, so neither the 36 h elapsed total nor the 5/3/4 h legs can be set; the stored legs look short against every account but no replacement is stated.

items.fact: total gain/loss: gain_ft vs itinerary vs approach prose
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. The live row now has gain_ft and loss_ft 2,138 (the net rise, road's end 3,480 ft to summit 5,618 ft), while the itinerary (gainFt/lossFt 3,400, totalNote 'roughly 3,400 ft') and the approach ('about 2.4 miles/3,900 ft one-way') still disagree. The 2025 report gives only the 3,480-5,618 ft range and 4.8 mi RT; the 2002 report describes small intermediate drops; peak-database ascent pages are behind a bot wall and the other searches return Grotto Mountain in Alberta. 2,138 ft is a floor, no source states a car-to-car total, and no two sources contradict 3,400 or 3,900 directly, so nothing is changed.

items.fact: Permit field names the Wild Sky Wilderness
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. Re-measured with the Forest Service wilderness boundary layer (with geometry): the crag pin lies OUTSIDE any wilderness, 165 m south of the Henry M. Jackson Wilderness boundary, and the ground height at the pin (4,758 ft, USGS 1 m DEM) fits the approach described for the crag (about 1,000 ft of gain from the hairpin pulloff), while the boundary point 165 m north is already at ~5,230 ft. Wild Sky Wilderness is more than 4 km away, so the Wild Sky name is certainly wrong. But no source states the crag's wilderness status or permit rule, and a 165 m margin is within the uncertainty of a guidebook-database pin, so the replacement text (no permit vs. a Henry M. Jackson self-issue permit) is still not settled; nothing patched. Suggested owner fix: drop the Wild Sky clause from `permit` so it agrees with access.permit 'N/A'.

items.fact: Mileage along the PCT to the stump/boot-path turnoff (4.6-5 mi vs 5.5-6 mi vs mile 5.75)
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. The new descriptions found place the stump turnoff by landmark and elevation only (about 1.5 mi beyond the second switchback, ~5,200 ft, a large stump on the left with the boot path 15 ft past it) and give no mileage from the trailhead; round-trip figures on record still range from 9.2 mi to ~11 mi. No two sources agree on the turnoff's mileage.

items.fact: Elevation of the glacier-exit / moat transition below the col
items.prior_evidence: New sources give no elevation for the moat: a 2004 report describes a short wet class 3 rock step beside a small waterfall into a cirque, then the glacier, and a sketchy moat crossing at the rock step below the main summit (no height); a route page puts the snow-finger exit at 4,800-5,000 ft and a waterfall near 5,100 ft. Neither states 6,200 or 6,500 ft for the moat. Side finding (pins out of scope): the USGS ground height at both the 'Snow gully and moat transition' pin and the 'Southeast ridge notch' pin is about 2,870 ft, so those pins are nowhere near the features they name.

items.fact: Total gain/loss: gain_ft 6,000 vs loss_ft 5,500 vs approach '~5,500 ft' on an out-and-back
items.prior_evidence: Third attempt. Archived copies of the Hourglass Gully route page and a Lake Serene trip report give only point elevations (Lake Serene ~2,251 ft, the gully base ~4,200 ft, the constriction ~5,000 ft, a schrund near 5,400 ft) and no cumulative gain; a 2013 party write-up gives none either. Stated totals remain 5,500 ft (club route page) and over 6,000 ft (one party), which disagree, so no figure is adopted.

items.fact: Elevation of the Waterfall 3 crux
items.prior_evidence: Third attempt. An archived route description of the South Gully puts Step 2 (a wet slab waterfall it calls its own crux) at about 3,400 ft and Step 3 (the jammed-boulder fall) at about 3,700 ft, with the gully reaching 4,000 ft just above it; this is the only source found that states the boulder-jam height, and it matches neither the prose's ~3,900 ft nor the waypoint's 3,600 ft. Another report's c.3,900 ft refers to a 20 ft tower, not clearly the same step, and the scramble-guide statement that the cave exit is 400-500 ft above the third falls would only yield a figure by subtraction. No two sources agree on the crux height, so nothing is changed.

items.fact: Waypoint distance jump at the summit
items.prior_evidence: Still real: the summit waypoint's distMi 16.92 (distFrom track) follows a chain that reaches the gully below the summit at 7.5 mi, while the itinerary (10.5 mi to camp), totalNote (~24 mi round trip) and dist_km (12 mi) disagree with both. Third-pass sources give only the Little Giant Pass leg (10.4 mi round trip / 4,100 ft to the pass) and a verbal description of the Napeequa continuation; no source states a one-way distance from the Little Giant trailhead to Berge's summit, and no two sources contradict 16.92 with a stated figure, so it is neither replaced nor nulled. The waypoint chain's own distances should be reviewed together with the pins.

items.fact: total elevation gain/loss
items.prior_evidence: Still real: gain_ft/loss_ft 8,400 vs itinerary days 7,000 and a totalNote of ~6,500. The 8,400 ft figure belongs to the Northeast Buttress with a Park Creek exit; a 2023 Southwest Couloir descent report (from Stehekin) gives only segment distances, and the other couloir figures found are for different approaches. No two sources give this route's gain by this approach.

items.fact: road-walk and One Acre Lake distances from the current gate
items.prior_evidence: Still real: waypoints put the second switchback at 2.25 mi and One Acre Lake at 3.7 mi, while the approach prose says ~6 mi to the lake and both bivy notes say a 5-6 mi road walk. Third-pass sources disagree in the same way: one scramble description gives 2.25 mi of closed road to the second switchback at 3,700 ft, another says about 5 miles of walking before leaving the road at ~3,700 ft. No two agree, so nothing is changed.

items.fact: The Obelisk's own elevation disagreement across waypoints
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. The live row still carries 4,494 ft on two Obelisk waypoints and high_point_ft, and 4,900 ft on a third whose note says it sits further up-slope than Sofa King Buttress. The crag database remains the only published record of the formation (4,494 ft, down the shoulder from Sofa King), and it contradicts that note, but the USGS 1 m ground model reads about 4,699 ft at its own coordinate on steep ground, so it does not confirm either figure. Searches for any guide, map name or trip report placing The Obelisk turned up nothing further. With one source for 4,494 and none for 4,900, neither value is changed.

items.fact: Fox Camp elevation (waypoint 6,900 ft) vs approach saying the basin (~7,100 ft) is ~1,000 ft above the junction
items.prior_evidence: Still no published elevation for Fox Camp. The USGS ground height where OpenStreetMap joins Trail #1437 to the Pyramid trail is ~6,587 ft, and at the row's Fox Camp pin ~5,728 ft; neither is a stated figure and they disagree with each other by ~850 ft, so the pin placement itself is in doubt. Trip write-ups checked (two Saska/Emerald reports) give mileages and whole-trip totals only. One topo reading with an uncertain point is not two sources; no patch.

items.fact: rock_grade undersells the technical climbing
items.prior_evidence: STRUCTURAL: the row mixes two lines (the East Ridge and the Balanced Rock obelisk). The East Ridge should win everywhere: grade should drop the 5.7 (e.g. 'Class 4, low 5th'), partner_requirements' 'sustained 5.7 trad leading' should become low-5th scrambling/leading, and the five pitch_detail rows graded 5.4-5.7 (crux placed on a tower below the obelisk) should be cleared or rewritten, since no source gives a pitch breakdown; the commitment numeral (grade says III, commitment II) has no source either. Sources: the peak's route page calls the East Ridge the easier route, mostly 4th with some low 5th, and gives 5.7 only for the Balanced Rock (shoulder stand to its E-side pedestal, bolt-protected friction); a 2005 East Ridge report quotes the route description as '4th and 5th class to 5.0' and found a 4th-class chimney and a harder chimney with a couple of single mid-5th moves; the encyclopedia entry gives the easiest route as class 4. rock_grade ('Class 3-4, short 5th-class moves') is therefore NOT undersold; the reader's proposed direction is wrong. Rewriting pitch rows is beyond a minimal patch, so no patch.

items.fact: total gain: gain_ft/loss_ft 5,200 vs itinerary/approach/totalNote 4,730
items.prior_evidence: Still present. A third search again surfaced only the single Southwest Spur listing (8.7 mi to Fish Creek Pass, 22 mi round trip, 5,200 ft) and the regional hike page (7.5 mi and 3,500 ft to Star Lake, then an off-trail scramble with no figure); multi-day Sawtooth traverses that include Star Peak give whole-trip totals. No second independent source states a Star Peak-only cumulative gain, and 4,730 (net relief) cannot be confirmed either. No patch.

items.fact: gain_ft/loss_ft (5,600) vs itinerary gain total and totalNote (5,400)
items.prior_evidence: An archived copy of the main peak page gives the Trail #641 round trip as 16 mi with 4,000+ ft cumulative gain from a 3,020 ft trailhead, which is the South Peak lookout, not North Peak. The only North Peak figure remains one report's 5,600 ft gained and lost over ~14 mi. No second source for either 5,600 or 5,400.

items.fact: Car-to-car distance: waypoint distMi (summit 2.7 mi one way) and itinerary 5.4 mi round trip look too long for the geometry
items.prior_evidence: The only summer Union-only figure found is the Mountaineers scramble page's 5.0 mi round trip / 2,400 ft (the gain implies a lower parking spot on Smithbrook Road than the trailhead); regional guides give 9.5-12 mi including Jove Peak or the winter road walk. No second source confirms a summer car-to-car figure from the Smithbrook Trailhead, so the waypoint distMi and itinerary miles are not changed.

sectionBreakdown.note: From the North Creek Trail trailhead on Twisp River Road, hike ~2 miles of trail, cross the creek onto the old mine trail, and climb ~1.5-2 miles up to the 7,680+ ft saddle just north…

cleared_value.notes: Gain the east ridge crest above the 8,000 ft notch and climb the first blocky steps on sound granite; mostly class 3-4 with occasional low-5th moves.
A steeper tower of solid granite just below the Sherpa Balanced Rock obelisk provides the technical crux - a short crack/corner move rated 5.7.
Continue over and around a series of towers along the crest, passing directly beneath the Balanced Rock feature; route-finding among blocks is the main challenge here.
Moderate, more broken climbing across sandy benches toward the base of the summit block.
Short final pitch up the summit pinnacle to the true summit; most parties then traverse to the West Ridge for the descent rather than reversing this route.
